title: How many lines and angles can three points make?
description: Three points that are not on one line are labelled A, B and C. A line is drawn through each pair of points, and the angles that the lines make at the points are named with a curve marked on each.
teaching_notes: One idea: each pair of points gives one line, and at each point two of those lines meet to make one angle. Watch for students who count the same line twice, such as AB and BA, or who forget one of the angles.

source: Mark any three points on your paper that are not on one line. Label them A, B, C. Draw all possible lines going through pairs of these points. How many lines do you get? Name them. How many angles can you name using A, B, C? Write them down, and mark each of them with a curve as in Fig. 2.9.
video_script.why: The child joins each pair of three points to get the lines, and names the angle at each point with the vertex in the middle.
video_script.substitution: Draw a line through each pair of the points A, B and C, and name the angle at each point with a curve.
video_script.anchor: a page with three points A, B and C that are not on one line
video_script.payoff_line: There are three lines and three angles

final_answer.value: There are 3 lines, AB, BC and CA, and 3 angles, angle ABC, angle BCA and angle CAB
final_answer.spoken: there are three lines, A B, B C and C eigh, and three angles, eigh B C, B C eigh and C eigh B

never_show: the count of the lines or of the angles, before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line is drawn through each pair of the points; the pairs are A and B, B and C, and C and A.
The lines are AB, BC and CA, and the line BA is the same line as AB, so it is not counted again.
The points are not on one line, so at each point two of the lines meet and make an angle.
The angle at B is ABC, the angle at C is BCA, and the angle at A is CAB, with the vertex as the middle letter.
So there are 3 lines and 3 angles.
video_script.design: One idea: join each pair of points to get the lines, then name the angle at each point. The three points stay on the board and the lines are drawn one at a time. The method is the same way as the examples in the book on the arms and the vertex of an angle.
